sentences.text: The holotype specimen, cataloged as IVPP 14010, contains an almost complete skull, lower jaws, parts of the forelimbs, fifteen vertebrae, and most of the ribcage.
This skull measures exactly 144 mm in length.
In life, the animal was likely about the size of a domestic cat.
The genus was described by James A. Clark and colleagues in 2004.
The name combines the Junggar Basin where it was found with the Greek word for crocodile.
The species name sloani honors C. Sloan, who discovered the holotype.
It possessed very little cranial kinesis and powerful jaw muscle attachment sites, traits similar to modern crocodilians.
Unlike the semi-aquatic movement of modern crocodilians, this animal was adapted for terrestrial locomotion.
A tall and narrow semicircular canal in its inner ear is an adaptation believed to aid in head orientation and gaze while on land.
Junggarsuchus lived during the Late Jurassic period, between 163.5 and 162.2 million years ago.
Fossils come from the lower member of the Shishugou Formation, dating from 164 to 159 million years ago.
It is debated whether the lack of osteoderms is due to taphonomic conditions or because the specimen was a juvenile.
The function of pneumatic spaces in the skull is debated; they may absorb shock or result from cranial sinus invasion.
The exact contact between the surangular and angular bones is uncertain, with possibilities ranging from short contact to significant contact similar to Dibothrosuchus.
